'''John Edward Norwood Veron''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|OAM}} (born 1945),  credited in research as '''J. E. N. Veron''', and in other writing as '''Charlie Veron''', is an Australian biologist, taxonomist, and specialist in the study of [[coral]]s and [[coral reef|reefs]].{{sfn|Veron|2017}} He has described 173 of the world's coral species.

==Early life and education ==
John Edward Norwood Veron (known as "Charlie" due to his interest in the natural sciences at school)<ref name=":1" /> was born in 1945 in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], Australia. He attended [[Barker College]] in Sydney.{{sfn|Veron|2017}}<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/lifestyle/charlie-veron-the-dire-environmental-prognosis-we-cannot-ignore-20170711-gx8tqr.html|title=Live near the beach? Coral reef expert Charlie Veron has some advice for you|last=Elliott|first=Tim|date=2017-07-14|website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald ]]|language=en|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref> 

He won a Commonwealth scholarship as a gifted student and went on study at the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]]. His main interests were in the natural world, especially marine life.{{sfn|Veron|2017}} He participated in the scuba club while at university.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Veron|first=John Edward Norwood|date=2001|title=Reflections|journal=Atoll Research Bulletin|volume=494|issue=6|pages=109–117|doi=10.5479/si.00775630.494-6.109}}</ref>

His honours thesis was on the behaviour of [[gliding possum]]s. He took his M.Sc. with a study on the temperature regulation of lizards. Veron completed his PhD with a study on the neurophysiology of dragonflies,<ref name=":0" /> awarded in 1971.<ref name =reef/>

== Career ==
After completing his PhD, Veron was offered a postdoctoral position at [[James Cook University]] to study corals.<ref name =reef>{{Cite book|title=Curating the Future| chapter-url= https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/e/9781315620770/chapters/10.4324/9781315620770-30|chapter=The reef in time: the prophecy of Charlie Veron's living collections In Curating the Future: Museums, Communities and Climate Change|last=McCalman|first=Iain| editor-first1=Jennifer| editor-first2=Libby| editor-first3=Kirsten| editor-last1=Newell| editor-last2=Robin| editor-last3=Wehner|date=2016|doi=10.4324/9781315620770 |isbn=9781315620770| s2cid=217533671|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref> He was the first full-time researcher on the [[Great Barrier Reef]] (1972) and the first scientist employed by the [[Australian Institute of Marine Science]] (1974). He participated in 67 expeditions to all the major reef provinces in the world. He credited "Red" Gilmartin and [[John W. Wells]] from [[Cornell University]] as key figures in clarifying his interest in taxonomy in the 1970s.<ref name=":0" />

Veron has named 173 reef corals and built a taxonomic framework for corals that is used throughout the world.<ref name="natgeo">{{Cite journal|last=McCalman|first=Iain|date=2014-04-15|title=The Great Coral Grief|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/explorer-pleads-to-save-the-great-barrier-reef|journal=Scientific American|language=en|volume=310|issue=5|pages=66–69|doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0514-66|pmid=24783594|bibcode=2014SciAm.310e..66M|issn=0036-8733|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He founded the [[Orpheus Island]] Marine Station. He introduced the concept of [[reticulate evolution]] to the field of coral taxonomy.{{sfn|Veron|2017}}

== Recognition ==
In 2009, Sir [[David Attenborough]] introduced Veron's lecture to the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/explorer-pleads-to-save-the-great-barrier-reef/|title=Explorer Pleads to Save the Great Barrier Reef|last=McCalman|first=Iain|date=2014|website=Scientific American}}</ref>

He was featured in the 2017 documentary ''[[Chasing Coral]]''.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

A sculpture of Veron, called "The Godfather of Coral", was created by [[Jason deCaires Taylor]] for the [[Museum of Underwater Art]] as part of the ''Ocean Sentinels'' above the surface exhibition in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mtq.qm.qld.gov.au/Events+and+Exhibitions/Exhibitions/2022/03/Ocean+Sentinels |title =Museum of Tropical Queensland (2022) Ocean Sentinels above the surface exhibition, Townsville}}</ref> 

He has received many professional awards, including:
* Scientific Diving Lifetime Achievement Award ([[American Academy of Underwater Sciences]]){{cn|date=November 2024}}
* Darwin Medal, 2004 ([[International Society for Reef Studies]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=Darwin Medal |url=https://coralreefs.org/awards-honors-fellowships/darwin-medal/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=International Coral Reef Society |language=en-US}}</ref>
* Silver Jubilee Pin (Australian Marine Sciences Association)<ref name="HUP">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hup.harvard.edu/catalog.php?isbn=9780674034976&content=reviews|title=(Reviews of) A Reef in Time — J.E.N. Veron |publisher= Harvard University Press|website=www.hup.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-26}}</ref>
*[[Order of Australia|Medal of the Order of Australia]] for "service to marine research", 2021<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr John Edward Veron|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2009396|access-date=2021-06-17|website=It's An Honour}}</ref>
*Ocean Sentinel sculpture ([[Museum of Underwater Art]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.moua.com.au/visit/ocean-sentinels/prof-john-charlie-veron|access-date=2024-04-22|title=Professor John (Charlie) Veron}}</ref>

==Other activities and achievements==
Since 2008 Veron and several colleagues have been producing an open access website about coral taxonomy, [[biogeography]] and identification, [[Corals of the World (website)|''Corals of The World'']]. The website includes a mapping program called Coral Geographic and an identification program called CoralID. 

He has campaigned extensively on climate change, mass [[coral bleaching|bleaching of coral reefs]], [[ocean acidification]], and related environmental issues.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

Veron has written many books and monographs about corals and coral reefs, including:

*{{Cite book|url={{google books |plainurl=y |id=m5zwAAAAMAAJ}}|title=Corals of the world|last=Veron|first=John Edward Norwood|date=2000|publisher=Australian Institute of Marine Science|language=en}}
*{{Cite book|url={{google books |plainurl=y |id=MowWAQAAIAAJ}}|title=Hermatypic corals of Japan|last=Veron|first=John Edward Norwood|date=1992|publisher=Australian Institute of Marine Science|isbn=9780642170835|language=en}}
*{{Cite book|url={{google books |plainurl=y |id=piQvtbFUicAC}}|title=Corals in Space and Time: The Biogeography and Evolution of the Scleractinia|last=Veron|first=John Edward Norwood|date=1995|publisher=Cornell University Press|isbn=0801482631|language=en}}
*{{Cite book|url={{google books |plainurl=y |id=QPIelpGvDBUC}}|title=Corals of Australia and the Indo-Pacific|last=Veron|first=John Edward Norwood|date=1993|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=9780824815042|language=en}}
*{{Cite book|url={{google books |plainurl=y |id=qOALAQAAIAAJ}}|title=Scleractinia of Eastern Australia|last1=Veron|first1=John Edward Norwood|last2=Pichon|first2=Michel|date=1976|publisher=Australian Government Publishing Service|isbn=9780642023209|language=en}}
